why: The criterion holds for all four verifier checks. Check 1's cases only test what "returns x limited to the range lo to hi" means: values below the range give lo, values above give hi, values inside give x, and the bounds count as inside (including [7,3,3]→3). It also checks that clamp is exported. Check 2 only requires that every call with lo greater than hi throws an instance of RangeError. Check 3 needs each exported function to be named in README.md and described there, which is what "documents" means; a substring match is looser than the words, not stricter. Check 4 needs exit 0 and no failing or cancelled tests, which is what "passes" means. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition)": whether clamp got its own tests, which files the PR changes, and NaN or non-number inputs. No mutation test, branch rule or exact-wording rule appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.
